thread:
meera: heads-up — noticed a spike of duplicate SAML assertion events in audit-ingest around the key rotation window, and a handful of KMS decrypt errors. looks like some downstream RBAC mapping jobs picked up stale attributes :thinking_face:

jordan: ugh. which idp/tenant? production? any correlation ids?

meera: idp=okta:corp, env=prod. 2:15–2:22 UTC window. see sample logs below — asserting signature verification failed twice then succeeded. also a few `kms.DecryptError` from audit-processor.

meera: ```
2026-03-23T02:15:04Z authsvc ERROR signature verify failed: key-id=key-prod-2026-03-23 old-kid=sha1:abcd1234
2026-03-23T02:15:05Z authsvc WARN retry verify succeeded: key-id=key-prod-2026-03-23 new-kid=ed25519:efgh5678
2026-03-23T02:16:09Z audit-processor ERROR kms.DecryptError: failed to unwrap envelope key: alias/okta-wrapping-prod not found
```

sam: deploy-bot posted a rotation earlier? @deploy-bot can you confirm scheduled rotation time for OKTA signing keys?

deploy-bot: automated rotation executed for `okta-signing-prod` at 2026-03-23T02:14:50Z. post-rotate hooks ran (wrap key alias swap). no rollback.

jordan: that lines up. looks like a brief window where services had mixture of old/new keys. but `alias/okta-wrapping-prod not found` sounds like an alias propagation issue to KMS replicas or IAM permission mismatch. did we push a new alias name?

meera: ops said alias unchanged, but HSM team replaced underlying key material with a new alias mapping during maintenance. running `aws kms describe-key` shows both keys but audit-processor IAM role couldn't ListAliases for the new alias due to a policy scoping change.

sam: ok. two-pronged impact then: (1) some authsvc verifications transiently got old kid vs new kid, causing duplicates in downstream audit logs when retries occurred; (2) audit-processor errored on decrypt and retried later, producing duplicate audit entries and short RBAC drift while mapping jobs reprocessed events.

oncall-ryan: I'm on it — will temporarily lift the alias scoping in the audit-processor role to allow ListAliases/GetKey for the new alias, and then re-run the failed jobs. patching now.

jordan: doing root-cause checklist:
- confirm rotation time and rotation messages (deploy-bot)
- check IAM policy diff for audit-processor role (meera)
- reprocess failed audit batches (oncall-ryan)
- verify no outstanding stale RBAC assignments (sam)

meera: IAM diff: changed resource constraint from `arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/*` to `arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789:key/okta-*` inadvertently, so new alias wasn't covered. rolling policy back to wildcard until we can deploy a scoped fix.

oncall-ryan: rollback IAM policy applied at 02:28 UTC. requeued 14 failed batches — processing. monitoring for duplicate dedupe issues in console metrics.

sam: good. two follow-ups before we close: (a) add a pre-rotation smoke check for alias visibility across all consumer roles, (b) add a brief client-side de-dup token on audit-processor to dedupe retries within a 60s window.

meera: agreed. I'll open a security RFC and assign owners. also adding an eval to Redwood Optimize to flag sudden audit ingest duplication spikes as a regression signal.

jordan: FYI — customers with long-lived sessions might have experienced a few 401s during that minute, but we have automatic retry/backoff. recommend a postmortem note in incidents later. :memo:

meera: thanks all. leaving this thread open for final reprocess confirmation. ping when requeue clears or if we need to roll back key again. :thumbsup:
